comparison.objective: Candidate adjusts a DRG 80 gripper opening-stop screw to 90°, locks the setting with a jam nut, and verifies retained opening through repeated cold-lever cycles. PR-757 inserts a cable to a controlled depth, closes a stripping station, and removes a measured length of insulation.
comparison.physical_skill: Candidate tests coaxial driver and thin-wrench seating, coupled screw/nut countertorque, preservation of an angular setting during locking, tool regrasping, and hands-off functional cycling. PR-757 tests cable alignment and depth insertion plus holding a spring-loaded cutting lever while pulling the cable through closed blades; the shared bimanual and lever primitives do not constitute the same ability.
comparison.success_condition: Candidate requires a locked opening within 3° of 90°, retained nuts, three return cycles within tolerance, at most 2° drift, tool withdrawal, and 30 mm clearance for one second, with explicit loss conditions. PR-757 requires 8–12 mm of insulation removed, the cut sleeve retained in the station, the lever released, and both grippers at least 40 mm clear, with partial credit for insertion or cutting. All available versions provide numeric rubric details.
comparison.reason: The tasks measure meaningfully different outcomes and mechanisms: preserving a mechanically adjusted stop against locknut reaction and proving retained articulation versus cutting and extracting cable insulation under sustained lever actuation.
